scientific_integrity: A self-contained analytical theorem for deterministic, identical, fully mixed strong-Allee patches. Exact algebraic identities were checked separately with rational arithmetic, and representative finite-mixing behavior was explored by numerical integration. The analytical proof, not numerical testing, supports universal quantifiers.
scientific_limitations: The parameter requirement is mixing rate greater than local cubic growth rate, not a claimed optimal synchronization threshold.
The exact majority-reversal sign law is for binary initially full/empty patch data; arbitrary initial data are covered by the general unique-threshold theorem and asymptotic moment expansion.
The expansion holds for fixed initial dimension and data as mixing-to-growth ratio tends to infinity; no uniformity in patch count is claimed.
Results are deterministic idealizations and are not field-validated predictions.
Historical priority cannot be certified; a related early paper was only accessible through its abstract.
title: Sharp majority reversal and skewness correction for strongly mixing Allee patches
